convention: Experimental course-only section boundaries and unscored response branches. Markdown thematic breaks separate sections; this is not an adopted course-spec component.

buy-the-ingredients.question: Which equipment detail would you like to check before gathering the ingredients?

responses.label: My specified pan and conventional oven are ready
responses.intro: With your specified pan and conventional oven ready, gather the ingredients and read their allergen labels.

responses.label: I want to check parchment versus wax paper
responses.intro: Use baking parchment, not wax paper, when lining this pan. Keep the parchment with your equipment as you gather the ingredients.

responses.label: My pan or oven differs
responses.intro: Pause before starting. Check the course equipment requirements and your oven manual; do not assume a different setup uses the same method.

buy-the-ingredients.question: What did you find when checking ingredient labels and equipment, and are you ready to prepare the oven?

responses.label: I checked the labels and have the ingredients and equipment
responses.intro: Your ingredient and equipment checks are recorded. Next, prepare the specified oven and pan.

responses.label: I still have a missing item or an unresolved allergy question
responses.intro: Stay with the ingredient list. Resolve missing items and allergy questions before proceeding; this draft has not tested substitutions.

buy-the-ingredients.videoPrompt: As the ingredient demonstration ends, which label or equipment check do you still need before preparing the oven?

preheat-the-oven.question: What will you check to decide whether the oven and pan are ready for batter?

responses.label: I will check the ready indicator and prepared pan
responses.intro: Check the preheated indicator and that the specified pan is greased and lined. Keep the workspace clear while you confirm readiness.

responses.label: I also have an oven thermometer
responses.intro: Use the preheated indicator and your oven thermometer as you check readiness. Confirm the conventional setting and prepared pan too.

preheat-the-oven.videoPrompt: As the oven demonstration ends, what will you check on the oven and prepared pan before mixing?

preheat-the-oven.question: Is the conventional oven at the specified setting with its ready indicator on, and is your pan prepared?

responses.label: The oven and pan are ready
responses.intro: With the oven and pan ready, measure the dry and wet ingredients for the batter.

responses.label: The oven is still warming or my pan is not ready
responses.intro: Wait for the ready indicator and finish preparing the specified pan. Keep this check open before mixing.

prepare-the-batter.question: What do you see after gently folding and scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl?

responses.label: No dry flour remains, but there are a few small lumps
responses.intro: A few small lumps are acceptable. In the next check, look for hidden dry flour rather than mixing for perfect smoothness.

responses.label: I can still see dry flour
responses.intro: Fold a few more times and scrape the sides and bottom, then look again. Do not move on while dry flour pockets remain.

responses.label: I want to understand why small lumps are acceptable
responses.intro: Extra mixing can make the cake tougher. Check for dry flour pockets, rather than beating out every small lump, in the final batter check.

prepare-the-batter.videoPrompt: As the folding demonstration ends, do you see dry flour or only small lumps, and what will you check next?

prepare-the-batter.question: After scraping the bowl, is your batter incorporated with no dry flour remaining and ready to go straight into the pan?

responses.label: I checked and my batter is ready
responses.intro: Your batter check is recorded. Pour it into the prepared pan and begin the baking step.

responses.label: The batter still seems dry or separated
responses.intro: Pause and review what you added. Keep this chapter open until the batter check is resolved.

bake-the-cake.question: What did the center and skewer show when you checked the cake?

responses.label: The center is set and the skewer has no wet batter
responses.intro: Your reported doneness check leads into safe removal and cooling. Use dry mitts and the heat-safe landing spot.

responses.label: The skewer still has wet batter
responses.intro: Bake another 3–5 minutes and check again as the draft describes. The timer and top color do not establish doneness.

bake-the-cake.videoPrompt: As the baking demonstration ends, what will the center and skewer need to show before you begin cooling?

bake-the-cake.question: What were the bake time and skewer result, and is the cake now completely cool before decorating?

responses.label: I reported the result and the cake is completely cool
responses.intro: With the cake completely cool, choose your frosting finish and read its label.

responses.label: The cake is still warm
responses.intro: Wait until the cake is completely cool. Keep this chapter open rather than frosting a warm cake.

decorate-the-cake.question: Which finish did you choose, and what made it work for your cooled cake?

responses.label: I chose a few swirls
responses.intro: Describe the swirls and how you spread the frosting gently. Include that choice in your result.

responses.label: I chose a sprinkle border
responses.intro: Describe your sprinkle border and check its label along with the frosting before sharing your result.

responses.label: I kept a simple smooth top
responses.intro: Describe the simple finish and how you spread it without tearing the cake. A photo is optional.

decorate-the-cake.videoPrompt: As the decorating demonstration ends, which finish would you choose and what label checks go with it?

decorate-the-cake.question: How would you describe your finished decoration and its label-based storage needs before serving?

responses.label: I described my finish and checked storage instructions
responses.intro: Your decoration and storage checks lead into asking guests about allergies before serving.

responses.label: I still need to check a frosting or decoration label
responses.intro: Read the frosting and decoration labels before continuing to serving.

serve-to-guests.question: Are you serving the cake now or preparing it for later, and what did you communicate about ingredients?

responses.label: I served it with the ingredient and allergy information
responses.intro: Since you served it now, reflect on what you observed and what you would change for the next bake.

responses.label: I prepared it for later and checked the storage label
responses.intro: Since you are serving later, keep following the frosting label for storage. Reflect on mixing and preparation without assuming guests have eaten it.

serve-to-guests.videoPrompt: As the serving demonstration ends, what allergy information will you share and are you serving now or later?

serve-to-guests.question: What would you change next time, and would you like to tidy up now or leave cleanup for later?

responses.label: I have a reflection and will tidy up now
responses.intro: Your reflection and reported serving checks are recorded. Check the oven is off and follow the cleanup and storage notes.

responses.label: I have a reflection and will tidy up later
responses.intro: Your reflection and reported serving checks are recorded. Cleanup remains optional; keep the oven off and follow storage instructions.
